hints.title: Server Availability State Tracking
hints.text: Maintain ready servers and busy servers separately, advancing system time to release completed servers.

hints.title: Priority by Weight and Index
hints.text: Order available servers primarily by weight and secondarily by index; order busy servers by finish time.

hints.title: Time Advancement on Empty Pool
hints.text: If no servers are available at task arrival time, advance the clock directly to the earliest completion time.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def assignTasks(self, servers: list[int], tasks: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        free = [(w, i) for i, w in enumerate(servers)]
        heapq.heapify(free)
        busy = []

        ans = []
        curr_time = 0

        for i, task_dur in enumerate(tasks):
            curr_time = max(curr_time, i)
            if not free and busy[0][0] > curr_time:
                curr_time = busy[0][0]

            while busy and busy[0][0] <= curr_time:
                _, w, s_idx = heapq.heappop(busy)
                heapq.heappush(free, (w, s_idx))

            w, s_idx = heapq.heappop(free)
            ans.append(s_idx)
            heapq.heappush(busy, (curr_time + task_dur, w, s_idx))

        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all servers for each task takes O(m * n) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual priority queues process all events in O((m + n) log n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate handles clock fast-forwarding when all servers are currently occupied.

solutions.approach: Dual priority queues for available and busy servers
